# Switchboard — make any web app run on the user's own AI

> Switchboard is a Mac app that brokers AI for web apps. Your page asks it for a completion,
> a tool call, or storage; a consent gate on the user's machine approves; you get the result.
> You never hold an API key, never pay for inference, never run a backend for it.
> An app that does this is called a **wrapp**.

If you are an agent wiring an app to Switchboard, this file is enough to do it.
Full spec: https://github.com/sameeeeeeep/switchboard/blob/main/docs/BUILDING-A-WRAPP.md

## What changes in your app

Replace your own model backend with the broker. That is the whole migration, and it needs
**no install** — Switchboard injects `window.claude` into the page.

```js
// before — your key, your bill, your server
const r = await fetch("/api/openai", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }) });

// after — the user's Claude (or their local model), no key, no server
await window.claude.request({ method: "claude_connect", params: {
  models: ["claude-haiku-4-5"],
  reason: "Rewrite the text you paste",     // shown in the consent popup
}});

const { text } = await window.claude.request({ method: "claude_complete", params: {
  prompt, model: "claude-haiku-4-5", maxTokens: 300,
}});
```

Wait for the provider before calling it — it is injected at document start, and fires an event:

```js
const ready = () => window.claude?.isRelay
  ? Promise.resolve(window.claude)
  : new Promise(r => window.addEventListener("claude#initialized", () => r(window.claude), { once: true }));
const claude = await ready();
```

> There is a typed wrapper (`@relay/sdk`, `getRelay` / `whenRelayReady`) used inside this repo, but it is
> **not published to npm yet** — so build against `window.claude.request` above, which is the same wire
> protocol and is what ships today.

## Where your app runs — read this before you deploy

Two ways a wrapp gets the bridge, and they have different rules:

| | How the bridge arrives | Origin rules |
|---|---|---|
| **Inside Switchboard** (a native window) | The Mac app injects it into whatever URL it loads | **Any origin. Your domain works today** — send users there with `switchboard://open?url=…` (above). |
| **A normal browser tab** | The Chrome extension injects it | Only an allowlist: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `thelastprompt.ai`, `sameep.ai`, `sameeeeeeep.github.io` |

What that means in practice:

- **Developing locally? It just works** — `localhost` is allowlisted, so a browser tab gets `window.claude`.
- **Deployed to your own domain?** It works when the user opens it **through Switchboard** (the native
  window bridges any origin). In a plain browser tab it will silently have no `window.claude` until your
  origin is added to the extension — open an issue to request it.
- **Always degrade honestly**: if `window.claude` is absent, say so and tell the user to open the app in
  Switchboard. Never fail silently.

## Getting the user into Switchboard — the standard button

**Use the canonical button. Do not hand-roll one** — every wrapp uses the same script so the
affordance looks and behaves identically everywhere, and improves in one place.

```html
<script src="https://thelastprompt.ai/switchboard/open-in-switchboard.js" defer></script>
<div data-switchboard-open></div>
```

That's the whole integration. The script handles all three states for you:

| State | What happens |
|---|---|
| Already inside Switchboard | Renders nothing — your app just works |
| Installed | `switchboard://open` hands **this page** to the Mac app: a native window, any origin, no Chrome extension, no allowlist. Switchboard asks the user first, naming your domain. |
| Not installed | Falls back to the download page after ~1.2s of nothing happening |

Options, as data-attributes on the mount element:

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `data-name` | `document.title` | The name shown in Switchboard's consent card |
| `data-url` | this page | The page to open |
| `data-label` | `Open in Switchboard` | Button text |
| `data-theme` | `dark` | `dark` or `light` |

Rendering your own UI instead? The script also exposes:

```js
window.openInSwitchboard({ url, name, onMissing });   // same handoff + fallback, your chrome
```

### The URL scheme, if you need it directly

```
switchboard://open?url=<encoded page url>&name=<encoded display name>
```

Only `http`/`https` targets are accepted, the user is always asked, and the card names the **host**.
Admission is not authorization: your model and tool grants are still requested separately inside.

### Show your app's state honestly

```js
const inSwitchboard = !!window.claude?.isRelay;
document.body.classList.toggle("needs-switchboard", !inSwitchboard);
```

Never fail silently. If there's no provider, show the button — don't let a dead AI feature look broken.

## The wire methods

`window.claude.request({ method, params })` → Promise. The methods:

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `claude_capabilities` | feature-detect; always allowed |
| `claude_connect` | request a scope (models / tools) — the consent popup |
| `claude_complete` | one-shot completion |
| `claude_stream` | streamed completion |
| `claude_listTools` · `claude_callTool` | list / call a granted tool |
| `claude_storage` | private per-app storage (`get`/`set`/`list`/`delete`/`bind`) |
| `claude_context` | shared cross-app context |
| `claude_speak` | on-device text-to-speech |
| `claude_permissions` · `claude_health` | current grant · is the daemon alive |

## The capability surface (BYOP 1.0.0 — all of it)

| What you want | How | Consent |
|---|---|---|
| Feature-detect | `relay.capabilities()` | none |
| One-shot completion | `relay.complete(params)` | within grant |
| Streamed completion | `for await (const d of relay.stream(params))` | within grant |
| Agentic (model uses tools) | `relay.complete({ ..., agentic: true })` | reads auto, writes prompt |
| List / call a tool | `relay.listTools()` · `relay.callTool(name, args)` | reads auto, writes prompt |
| Private local storage | `relay.storage.get/set/list/delete` | free |
| Bind storage to a real folder | `relay.storage.bind(path)` | always prompts |
| Shared cross-app context | `relay.context.publish/active/pick` | user picks |
| Local text-to-speech | `relay.speak(text)` | within grant, on-device |
| Who the user is | `relay.identity()` | display name only |

### Streaming

```js
for await (const d of relay.stream({ prompt })) {
  if (d.type === "text")    append(d.text);
  if (d.type === "sources") cite(d.urls);
  if (d.type === "done")    finish(d.result);
}
```

Use `messages: [{ role, content }, …]` instead of `prompt` for multi-turn, `attachments` for images,
and a stable `sessionId` to reuse a warm thread across many calls.

### Agentic + tools

`agentic: true` lets the model call your granted tools mid-reasoning. You don't implement the gate:
**reads run silently within scope, writes pop a consent the user clicks.** `res.toolCalls` reports
what ran and how each resolved. Or drive one yourself: `relay.callTool("WebSearch", { query })`.

### Storage

Per-app, isolated to your origin — no other wrapp can read it. Values are opaque strings; store JSON.

```js
await relay.storage.set("workspace", JSON.stringify(state));
const raw = await relay.storage.get("workspace");   // string | null
await relay.storage.bind("~/Documents/my-app/.data"); // one consent, shows the path
```

**Keys are filenames.** A key maps 1:1 to `<folder>/<key>.json` and must match
`/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$/`. Namespace with `-`, never `:` — a colon is illegal in NTFS
filenames and the write silently does nothing.

## What you get, and what you give up

You get: the user's model (Claude or a local one), their connected tools, their project context,
local storage, TTS — with no key, no inference bill, and no backend.

You give up: holding their credentials or data. You can't widen your granted scope from a system
prompt, and you never see their keys. That constraint is the product.

## Checklist

- [ ] Call `window.claude.request({ method, params })` (the SDK wrapper isn't on npm yet)
- [ ] `connect()` declaring the exact model + tool strings you invoke
- [ ] Handle a partial grant
- [ ] Storage keys are filename-safe (`-`, never `:`)
- [ ] Degrade honestly when `window.claude` is absent — tell the user to open it in Switchboard
- [ ] Ship the canonical button (`open-in-switchboard.js`) — never a hand-rolled copy
- [ ] Deploying to your own domain? It works inside Switchboard; a plain browser tab needs your origin allowlisted
